original_question: Which chromosome contains the gene whose homozygous mutation leads to a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy potentially responsive to mevalonolactone?

final_qi.question: Which chromosome contains the gene whose homozygous mutation leads to a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy potentially responsive to mevalonolactone?
final_qi.long_answer: A recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy has been traced to homozygous loss-of-function mutations in the HMGCR gene, which encodes 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-glutaryl-CoA reductase. Because HMGCR produces mevalonate, patients may improve when given the downstream metabolite mevalonolactone. The HMGCR gene is situated at 5q13.3, meaning the responsible gene resides on chromosome 5.

final_answer.long_answer: The recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy responsive to mevalonolactone is caused by homozygous loss-of-function mutations in HMGCR, the gene for 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-glutaryl-CoA reductase, a key enzyme of the mevalonate pathway. HMGCR is located at 5q13.3 on chromosome 5, so chromosome 5 contains the gene whose homozygous mutation produces this treatable LGMD phenotype.
